title: E-commerce: DesiCart Marketplace
description: DesiCart is a fictional Indian online marketplace selling electronics, fashion, home goods, beauty, grocery and books across 20 cities. The data covers two years of customers, orders, line items, payments and returns (Jan 2023 to Dec 2024), including festive-season sale spikes around Diwali and the usual messiness of a real order database. Use it for revenue analysis, cohort and repeat-purchase analysis, return analysis and cleaning practice.

tables.name: customers
tables.description: One row per registered customer (a few duplicated rows are deliberate).

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer identifier (primary key, chronological by signup)

columns.name: city
columns.description: Home city (inconsistent casing/whitespace, NULL for some)

columns.name: state
columns.description: Indian state of the city (NULL when city is NULL)

columns.name: signup_date_raw
columns.description: Signup date as typed in a legacy form: mixed formats, some NULL (for cleaning lessons)

columns.name: acquisition_channel
columns.description: Marketing channel that brought the customer

columns.name: is_prime
columns.description: 1 if customer holds the paid DesiCart Prime membership

columns.name: category
columns.description: Top-level category (a few rows have inconsistent casing/whitespace)

tables.name: orders
tables.description: One row per order (about 1% exact duplicate rows are deliberate).

columns.name: order_date
columns.description: Date the order was placed (clean ISO in SQLite)

columns.name: order_time
columns.description: Time of day the order was placed (HH:MM:SS)

columns.name: order_status
columns.description: Delivered, Cancelled or RTO (return to origin, mostly COD)

columns.name: sales_channel
columns.description: Android App, iOS App, Website or Mobile Web

columns.name: total_amount
columns.description: Order value in INR after discount and shipping

columns.name: unit_price
columns.description: Selling price per unit in INR after discount (a few 100x outliers)

tables.name: payments
tables.description: Payment attempts (some orders have a failed attempt followed by a success).

columns.name: payment_method
columns.description: UPI, Credit Card, Debit Card, COD, Netbanking or Wallet

columns.name: payment_date
columns.description: Date of payment (delivery date for COD)

qualityIssues: orders: ~1% of rows (about 100) are exact duplicates (same order_id repeated); so orders.order_id has no PRIMARY KEY constraint.
customers: 20 exact duplicate customer rows; customers.customer_id is therefore not unique.
customers.email is NULL for ~8% of rows, phone ~3%, gender ~4%, city ~3% (state is NULL whenever city is NULL).
customers.city: ~10% of values have inconsistent casing or stray whitespace ('mumbai', ' Mumbai', 'DELHI ').
customers.signup_date_raw: free-text dates in four formats (YYYY-MM-DD, DD/MM/YYYY, '5 Mar 2023', 'Mar 5, 2023') and ~3% NULL; signup_date holds the clean value.
products.category: ~2% of values have inconsistent casing or whitespace.
order_items.unit_price: 12 rows are 100x too high (entry errors) which inflates order totals for those orders.
CSV only - orders.order_date: ~18% of rows are written as DD-MM-YYYY instead of YYYY-MM-DD.
CSV only - orders.total_amount: ~12% of rows are text like '₹1,234.50' (symbol and thousands commas).
CSV only - returns.refund_amount: ~50% of rows are text with rupee symbol and Indian digit grouping (e.g. '₹1,23,456.00').
payments: ~5% of online-paid orders have an extra earlier 'Failed' attempt row, so order_id is not unique in payments.

signals: [Instructor note] Festive spikes: order volume rises ~1.5-1.9x in the Diwali windows (Oct 8-16 2023, Nov 6-14 2023, Sep 27-Oct 6 2024, Oct 24-Nov 3 2024); weekends are ~18% higher; steady growth through 2024.
[Instructor note] Fashion and Footwear have return rates of ~21% and ~15% (mostly 'Size / fit issue'), versus ~1% for Grocery.
[Instructor note] COD orders are cancelled ~11% of the time and RTO another ~7%, versus ~3.5% cancellation for prepaid.
[Instructor note] Tier-2 cities use COD far more (~34% vs ~18%) and have longer delivery times.
[Instructor note] Prime members (22% of customers) place roughly twice the orders; customer activity is heavy-tailed (a minority of customers drive most orders).
[Instructor note] Data-entry outliers (12 order_items with 100x unit_price) distort average order value unless handled.
